subtitle: Lesson 4 · The Real Tradeoffs

eyebrow: A second axis of scoping: knowledge
code:
WHITE-BOX   full source/architecture/credentials
            fastest, thorough, least realistic of an attacker

GRAY-BOX    partial knowledge (e.g. standard user credentials)
            realistic insider/compromised-account scenario

BLACK-BOX   zero prior knowledge
            most realistic external-attacker simulation,
            most time-consuming, coverage risk
caption: Decided during scoping — not on day one of testing.

steps.label: Mirrors a genuinely common threat
steps.sub: an insider or a compromised low-privilege account

steps.label: No time wasted on recon a real attacker wouldn't need
steps.sub: covers more ground than black-box in the same window

steps.label: Far more realistic than white-box
steps.sub: without the full coverage guarantee white-box provides

steps.label: "Could a random attacker with nothing get in?"
steps.sub: request black-box, and budget the time it takes

subtitle: Authorization, scope, methodology, and knowledge model are all settled — now the real work begins.
